summary: preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes an obfuscated sibling bundle unrelated to declared purpose
details: The package advertises itself as an i18n configuration helper but its preinstall hook (node setup.mjs) downloads the Bun runtime from github.com/oven-sh/bun releases (bun-v1.3.13) into a temporary directory and uses it to execFileSync a sibling file, math_init.js, at install time. math_init.js is a ~727 KB single-line bun-cjs bundle with a shuffled numeric/string constants array and a rotation function (WV8StW), consistent with an obfuscator.io-style protected loader; no readable source for it ships in the tarball. setup.mjs itself uses hex-obfuscated identifier aliasing (_0x488df8=fs, _0x52943e=https, _0x548d91=zlib) and per-call inline lookup objects to hide calls to execFileSync, https.get, fs.readFileSync, and zlib. A second language runtime is unrelated to i18n configuration, and the executed payload's contents cannot be inspected from the shipped source. This is the alternate-runtime-dropper pattern: a Node-oriented package that stages a Bun runtime specifically to execute an opaque bundle out of the reach of Node-oriented scanners on every npm install.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
